subject.title: Feature: Inter-session progress streaming for sessions_send (ACP/long-running session support)

question: Should OpenClaw add a cross-session run-progress observation API for `sessions_send`, and should the public surface be `sessions_subscribe`, a `sessions_send` option, or a lower-level gateway event API first?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the API shape, authorization boundary, redaction model, buffering/retention policy, replay behavior, and channel delivery semantics are product and security decisions rather than a safe autonomous fix.

options.title: Add sessions_subscribe over bounded agent.events
options.body: Add a permission-checked `agent.events` read API with bounded replay/redaction and expose it through a separate `sessions_subscribe` tool for delegated runs.

options.title: Start with gateway event API only
options.body: Define and test the lower-level buffered event contract first, then decide the agent tool surface after the security model is stable.

options.title: Defer progress streaming
options.body: Keep `sessions_send` final-only for now and direct users to `timeoutSeconds: 0`, `sessions_history`, and completion announce behavior.

recommendation.title: Add sessions_subscribe over bounded agent.events
recommendation.body: Add a permission-checked `agent.events` read API with bounded replay/redaction and expose it through a separate `sessions_subscribe` tool for delegated runs.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has the strongest history across sessions_send, run-wait helpers, and adjacent gateway event surfaces.
